description:
About the Scholarship

IMSOGLO is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master in soil systems under global change, coordinated from Ghent University with European partners. Applications for the September 2027 intake opened on 1 October 2026; the scholarship round closes on 28 February 2027, and self-funded documents can follow until 31 May 2027.

OpportunityIMSOGLO – International Master in Soils and Global Change (Erasmus Mundus)
HostIMSOGLO Consortium (Ghent University)
LocationGhent (multi-country mobility), Belgium
Study LevelMaster's
FundingFully Funded
Stipend€1,400/month (EMJM scholarship rate)
Application Deadline28 February 2027
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

IMSOGLO is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master in soil systems under global change, coordinated from Ghent University with European partners. Applications for the September 2027 intake opened on 1 October 2026; the scholarship round closes on 28 February 2027, and self-funded documents can follow until 31 May 2027.

Programme Highlights

  • Ghent-coordinated soil science programme with a global-change lens
  • Scholarship deadline 28 February 2027; long self-funded tail to 31 May
  • Fieldwork across European soil observatories and partner universities
  • Careers in land management, climate services and environmental consulting

Who Should Apply

Bachelor's degrees (180 ECTS) in environmental science, biology, agriculture, geology or engineering are expected, with English documentation per the Ghent process.

Funding and Costs

Erasmus Mundus scholarships for selected students: tuition coverage plus monthly allowance.

Deadline and How to Apply

Apply through the Ghent University portal linked on the IMSOGLO site and complete legalised documents in time for the May stage. Key deadline information: 28 February 2027 (scholarship round); applications opened 1 October 2026; non-scholarship documents until 31 May 2027.

Official Link

  • Official application page (verified link)

About IMSOGLO Consortium (Ghent University)

The IMSOGLO consortium is coordinated by Ghent University and delivers the International Master of Science in Soils and Global Change with European partner universities.

Official website: https://imsoglo.eu

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 28 February 2027 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
